paragraphs.text: Then there come to Jesus from Jerusalem Pharisees and scribes, saying,
paragraphs.original: Τότε προσέρχονται τῷ Ἰησοῦ ἀπὸ Ἱεροσολύμων Φαρισαῖοι καὶ γραμματεῖς λέγοντες
paragraphs.translit: Tote proserchontai tō Iēsou apo Hierosolymōn Pharisaioi kai grammateis legontes

paragraphs.text: Why do thy disciples transgress the tradition of the elders? for they wash not their hands when they eat bread.
paragraphs.original: Διὰ τί οἱ μαθηταί σου παραβαίνουσιν τὴν παράδοσιν τῶν πρεσβυτέρων; οὐ γὰρ νίπτονται τὰς χεῖρας αὐτῶν ὅταν ἄρτον ἐσθίωσιν.
paragraphs.translit: Dia ti hoi mathētai sou parabainousin tēn paradosin tōn presbyterōn; ou gar niptontai tas cheiras autōn hotan arton esthiōsin.

paragraphs.text: And he answered and said unto them, Why do ye also transgress the commandment of God because of your tradition?
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Διὰ τί καὶ ὑμεῖς παραβαίνετε τὴν ἐντολὴν τοῦ θεοῦ διὰ τὴν παράδοσιν ὑμῶν;
paragraphs.translit: ho de apokritheis eipen autois· Dia ti kai hymeis parabainete tēn entolēn tou theou dia tēn paradosin hymōn;

paragraphs.text: For God said, Honor thy father and thy mother: and, He that speaketh evil of father or mother, let him die the death.
paragraphs.original: ὁ γὰρ θεὸς εἶπεν· Τίμα τὸν πατέρα καὶ τὴν μητέρα, καί· Ὁ κακολογῶν πατέρα ἢ μητέρα θανάτῳ τελευτάτω·
paragraphs.translit: ho gar theos eipen· Tima ton patera kai tēn mētera, kai· Ho kakologōn patera ē mētera thanatō teleutatō·

paragraphs.text: But ye say, whosoever shall say to his father or his mother, That wherewith thou mightest have been profited by me is given [to God];
paragraphs.original: ὑμεῖς δὲ λέγετε· Ὃς ἂν εἴπῃ τῷ πατρὶ ἢ τῇ μητρί· Δῶρον ὃ ἐὰν ἐξ ἐμοῦ ὠφεληθῇς,
paragraphs.translit: hymeis de legete· Hos an eipē tō patri ē tē mētri· Dōron ho ean ex emou ōphelēthēs,

paragraphs.text: he shall not honor his father. And ye have made void the word of God because of your tradition.
paragraphs.original: οὐ μὴ τιμήσει τὸν πατέρα αὐτοῦ· καὶ ἠκυρώσατε τὸν λόγον τοῦ θεοῦ διὰ τὴν παράδοσιν ὑμῶν.
paragraphs.translit: ou mē timēsei ton patera autou· kai ēkyrōsate ton logon tou theou dia tēn paradosin hymōn.

paragraphs.text: Ye hypocrites, well did Isaiah prophesy of you, saying,
paragraphs.original: ὑποκριταί, καλῶς ἐπροφήτευσεν περὶ ὑμῶν Ἠσαΐας λέγων·
paragraphs.translit: hypokritai, kalōs eprophēteusen peri hymōn Ēsaias legōn·

paragraphs.text: This people honoreth me with their lips; But their heart is far from me.
paragraphs.original: Ὁ λαὸς οὗτος τοῖς χείλεσίν με τιμᾷ, ἡ δὲ καρδία αὐτῶν πόρρω ἀπέχει ἀπʼ ἐμοῦ·
paragraphs.translit: Ho laos houtos tois cheilesin me tima, hē de kardia autōn porrō apechei apʼ emou·

paragraphs.text: But in vain do they worship me, Teaching [as their] doctrines the precepts of men.
paragraphs.original: μάτην δὲ σέβονταί με, διδάσκοντες διδασκαλίας ἐντάλματα ἀνθρώπων.
paragraphs.translit: matēn de sebontai me, didaskontes didaskalias entalmata anthrōpōn.

paragraphs.text: And he called to him the multitude, and said unto them, Hear, and understand:
paragraphs.original: Καὶ προσκαλεσάμενος τὸν ὄχλον εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Ἀκούετε καὶ συνίετε·
paragraphs.translit: Kai proskalesamenos ton ochlon eipen autois· Akouete kai syniete·

paragraphs.text: Not that which entereth into the mouth defileth the man; but that which proceedeth out of the mouth, this defileth the man.
paragraphs.original: οὐ τὸ εἰσερχόμενον εἰς τὸ στόμα κοινοῖ τὸν ἄνθρωπον, ἀλλὰ τὸ ἐκπορευόμενον ἐκ τοῦ στόματος τοῦτο κοινοῖ τὸν ἄνθρωπον.
paragraphs.translit: ou to eiserchomenon eis to stoma koinoi ton anthrōpon, alla to ekporeuomenon ek tou stomatos touto koinoi ton anthrōpon.

paragraphs.text: Then came the disciples, and said unto him, Knowest thou that the Pharisees were offended, when they heard this saying?
paragraphs.original: Τότε προσελθόντες οἱ μαθηταὶ λέγουσιν αὐτῷ· Οἶδας ὅτι οἱ Φαρισαῖοι ἀκούσαντες τὸν λόγον ἐσκανδαλίσθησαν;
paragraphs.translit: Tote proselthontes hoi mathētai legousin autō· Oidas hoti hoi Pharisaioi akousantes ton logon eskandalisthēsan;

paragraphs.text: But he answered and said, Every plant which my heavenly Father planted not, shall be rooted up.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν· Πᾶσα φυτεία ἣν οὐκ ἐφύτευσεν ὁ πατήρ μου ὁ οὐράνιος ἐκριζωθήσεται.
paragraphs.translit: ho de apokritheis eipen· Pasa phyteia hēn ouk ephyteusen ho patēr mou ho ouranios ekrizōthēsetai.

paragraphs.text: Let them alone: they are blind guides. And if the blind guide the blind, both shall fall into a pit.
paragraphs.original: ἄφετε αὐτούς· τυφλοί εἰσιν ὁδηγοὶ τυφλῶν· τυφλὸς δὲ τυφλὸν ἐὰν ὁδηγῇ, ἀμφότεροι εἰς βόθυνον πεσοῦνται.
paragraphs.translit: aphete autous· typhloi eisin hodēgoi typhlōn· typhlos de typhlon ean hodēgē, amphoteroi eis bothynon pesountai.

paragraphs.text: And Peter answered and said unto him, Declare unto us the parable.
paragraphs.original: Ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ Πέτρος εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Φράσον ἡμῖν τὴν παραβολὴν ταύτην.
paragraphs.translit: Apokritheis de ho Petros eipen autō· Phrason hēmin tēn parabolēn tautēn.

paragraphs.text: And he said, Are ye also even yet without understanding?
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν· Ἀκμὴν καὶ ὑμεῖς ἀσύνετοί ἐστε;
paragraphs.translit: ho de eipen· Akmēn kai hymeis asynetoi este;

paragraphs.text: Perceive ye not, that whatsoever goeth into the mouth passeth into the belly, and is cast out into the draught?
paragraphs.original: οὐ νοεῖτε ὅτι πᾶν τὸ εἰσπορευόμενον εἰς τὸ στόμα εἰς τὴν κοιλίαν χωρεῖ καὶ εἰς ἀφεδρῶνα ἐκβάλλεται;
paragraphs.translit: ou noeite hoti pan to eisporeuomenon eis to stoma eis tēn koilian chōrei kai eis aphedrōna ekballetai;

paragraphs.text: But the things which proceed out of the mouth come forth out of the heart; and they defile the man.
paragraphs.original: τὰ δὲ ἐκπορευόμενα ἐκ τοῦ στόματος ἐκ τῆς καρδίας ἐξέρχεται, κἀκεῖνα κοινοῖ τὸν ἄνθρωπον.
paragraphs.translit: ta de ekporeuomena ek tou stomatos ek tēs kardias exerchetai, kakeina koinoi ton anthrōpon.

paragraphs.text: For out of the heart come forth evil thoughts, murders, adulteries, fornications, thefts, false witness, railings:
paragraphs.original: ἐκ γὰρ τῆς καρδίας ἐξέρχονται διαλογισμοὶ πονηροί, φόνοι, μοιχεῖαι, πορνεῖαι, κλοπαί, ψευδομαρτυρίαι, βλασφημίαι.
paragraphs.translit: ek gar tēs kardias exerchontai dialogismoi ponēroi, phonoi, moicheiai, porneiai, klopai, pseudomartyriai, blasphēmiai.

paragraphs.text: these are the things which defile the man; but to eat with unwashen hands defileth not the man.
paragraphs.original: ταῦτά ἐστιν τὰ κοινοῦντα τὸν ἄνθρωπον, τὸ δὲ ἀνίπτοις χερσὶν φαγεῖν οὐ κοινοῖ τὸν ἄνθρωπον.
paragraphs.translit: tauta estin ta koinounta ton anthrōpon, to de aniptois chersin phagein ou koinoi ton anthrōpon.

paragraphs.text: And Jesus went out thence, and withdrew into the parts of Tyre and Sidon.
paragraphs.original: Καὶ ἐξελθὼν ἐκεῖθεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἀνεχώρησεν εἰς τὰ μέρη Τύρου καὶ Σιδῶνος.
paragraphs.translit: Kai exelthōn ekeithen ho Iēsous anechōrēsen eis ta merē Tyrou kai Sidōnos.

paragraphs.text: And behold, a Canaanitish woman came out from those borders, and cried, saying, Have mercy on me, O Lord, thou son of David; my daughter is grievously vexed with a demon.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἰδοὺ γυνὴ Χαναναία ἀπὸ τῶν ὁρίων ἐκείνων ἐξελθοῦσα ἔκραζεν λέγουσα· Ἐλέησόν με, κύριε υἱὸς Δαυίδ· ἡ θυγάτηρ μου κακῶς δαιμονίζεται.
paragraphs.translit: kai idou gynē Chananaia apo tōn horiōn ekeinōn exelthousa ekrazen legousa· Eleēson me, kyrie hyios Dauid· hē thygatēr mou kakōs daimonizetai.

paragraphs.text: But he answered her not a word. And his disciples came and besought him, saying, Send her away; for she crieth after us.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ οὐκ ἀπεκρίθη αὐτῇ λόγον. καὶ προσελθόντες οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ ἠρώτουν αὐτὸν λέγοντες· Ἀπόλυσον αὐτήν, ὅτι κράζει ὄπισθεν ἡμῶν.
paragraphs.translit: ho de ouk apekrithē autē logon. kai proselthontes hoi mathētai autou ērōtoun auton legontes· Apolyson autēn, hoti krazei opisthen hēmōn.

paragraphs.text: But he answered and said, I was not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Israel.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν· Οὐκ ἀπεστάλην εἰ μὴ εἰς τὰ πρόβατα τὰ ἀπολωλότα οἴκου Ἰσραήλ.
paragraphs.translit: ho de apokritheis eipen· Ouk apestalēn ei mē eis ta probata ta apolōlota oikou Israēl.

paragraphs.text: But she came and worshipped him, saying, Lord, help me.
paragraphs.original: ἡ δὲ ἐλθοῦσα προσεκύνει αὐτῷ λέγουσα· Κύριε, βοήθει μοι.
paragraphs.translit: hē de elthousa prosekynei autō legousa· Kyrie, boēthei moi.

paragraphs.text: And he answered and said, It is not meet to take the children`s bread and cast it to the dogs.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν· Οὐκ ἔστιν καλὸν λαβεῖν τὸν ἄρτον τῶν τέκνων καὶ βαλεῖν τοῖς κυναρίοις.
paragraphs.translit: ho de apokritheis eipen· Ouk estin kalon labein ton arton tōn teknōn kai balein tois kynariois.

paragraphs.text: But she said, Yea, Lord: for even the dogs eat of the crumbs which fall from their masters` table.
paragraphs.original: ἡ δὲ εἶπεν· Ναί, κύριε, καὶ γὰρ τὰ κυνάρια ἐσθίει ἀπὸ τῶν ψιχίων τῶν πιπτόντων ἀπὸ τῆς τραπέζης τῶν κυρίων αὐτῶν.
paragraphs.translit: hē de eipen· Nai, kyrie, kai gar ta kynaria esthiei apo tōn psichiōn tōn piptontōn apo tēs trapezēs tōn kyriōn autōn.

paragraphs.text: Then Jesus answered and said unto her, O woman, great is thy faith: be it done unto thee even as thou wilt. And her daughter was healed from that hour.
paragraphs.original: τότε ἀποκριθεὶς ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτῇ· Ὦ γύναι, μεγάλη σου ἡ πίστις· γενηθήτω σοι ὡς θέλεις. καὶ ἰάθη ἡ θυγάτηρ αὐτῆς ἀπὸ τῆς ὥρας ἐκείνης.
paragraphs.translit: tote apokritheis ho Iēsous eipen autē· Ō gynai, megalē sou hē pistis· genēthētō soi hōs theleis. kai iathē hē thygatēr autēs apo tēs hōras ekeinēs.

paragraphs.text: And Jesus departed thence, and came nigh unto the sea of Galilee; and he went up into the mountain, and sat there.
paragraphs.original: Καὶ μεταβὰς ἐκεῖθεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἦλθεν παρὰ τὴν θάλασσαν τῆς Γαλιλαίας, καὶ ἀναβὰς εἰς τὸ ὄρος ἐκάθητο ἐκεῖ.
paragraphs.translit: Kai metabas ekeithen ho Iēsous ēlthen para tēn thalassan tēs Galilaias, kai anabas eis to oros ekathēto ekei.

paragraphs.text: And there came unto him great multitudes, having with them the lame, blind, dumb, maimed, and many others, and they cast them down at this feet; and he healed them:
paragraphs.original: καὶ προσῆλθον αὐτῷ ὄχλοι πολλοὶ ἔχοντες μεθʼ ἑαυτῶν κωφούς, τυφλούς, χωλούς, κυλλούς, καὶ ἑτέρους πολλούς, καὶ ἔρριψαν αὐτοὺς παρὰ τοὺς πόδας αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἐθεράπευσεν αὐτούς·
paragraphs.translit: kai prosēlthon autō ochloi polloi echontes methʼ heautōn kōphous, typhlous, chōlous, kyllous, kai heterous pollous, kai erripsan autous para tous podas autou, kai etherapeusen autous·

paragraphs.text: insomuch that the multitude wondered, when they saw the dumb speaking, the maimed whole, and lame walking, and the blind seeing: and they glorified the God of Israel.
paragraphs.original: ὥστε τὸν ὄχλον θαυμάσαι βλέποντας κωφοὺς λαλοῦντας κυλλοὺς ὑγιεῖς καὶ χωλοὺς περιπατοῦντας καὶ τυφλοὺς βλέποντας· καὶ ἐδόξασαν τὸν θεὸν Ἰσραήλ.
paragraphs.translit: hōste ton ochlon thaumasai blepontas kōphous lalountas kyllous hygieis kai chōlous peripatountas kai typhlous blepontas· kai edoxasan ton theon Israēl.

paragraphs.text: And Jesus called unto him his disciples, and said, I have compassion on the multitude, because they continue with me now three days and have nothing to eat: and I would not send them away fasting, lest haply they faint on the way.
paragraphs.original: Ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς προσκαλεσάμενος τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ εἶπεν· Σπλαγχνίζομαι ἐπὶ τὸν ὄχλον, ὅτι ἤδη ἡμέραι τρεῖς προσμένουσίν μοι καὶ οὐκ ἔχουσιν τί φάγωσιν· καὶ ἀπολῦσαι αὐτοὺς νήστεις οὐ θέλω, μήποτε ἐκλυθῶσιν ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ.
paragraphs.translit: Ho de Iēsous proskalesamenos tous mathētas autou eipen· Splanchnizomai epi ton ochlon, hoti ēdē hēmerai treis prosmenousin moi kai ouk echousin ti phagōsin· kai apolysai autous nēsteis ou thelō, mēpote eklythōsin en tē hodō.

paragraphs.text: And the disciples say unto him, Whence should we have so many loaves in a desert place as to fill so great a multitude?
paragraphs.original: καὶ λέγουσιν αὐτῷ οἱ μαθηταί· Πόθεν ἡμῖν ἐν ἐρημίᾳ ἄρτοι τοσοῦτοι ὥστε χορτάσαι ὄχλον τοσοῦτον;
paragraphs.translit: kai legousin autō hoi mathētai· Pothen hēmin en erēmia artoi tosoutoi hōste chortasai ochlon tosouton;

paragraphs.text: And Jesus said unto them, How many loaves have ye? And they said, Seven, and a few small fishes.
paragraphs.original: καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Πόσους ἄρτους ἔχετε; οἱ δὲ εἶπαν· Ἑπτά, καὶ ὀλίγα ἰχθύδια.
paragraphs.translit: kai legei autois ho Iēsous· Posous artous echete; hoi de eipan· Hepta, kai oliga ichthydia.

paragraphs.text: And he commanded the multitude to sit down on the ground;
paragraphs.original: καὶ παραγγείλας τῷ ὄχλῳ ἀναπεσεῖν ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν
paragraphs.translit: kai parangeilas tō ochlō anapesein epi tēn gēn

paragraphs.text: and he took the seven loaves and the fishes; and he gave thanks and brake, and gave to the disciples, and the disciples to the multitudes.
paragraphs.original: ἔλαβεν τοὺς ἑπτὰ ἄρτους καὶ τοὺς ἰχθύας καὶ εὐχαριστήσας ἔκλασεν καὶ ἐδίδου τοῖς μαθηταῖς οἱ δὲ μαθηταὶ τοῖς ὄχλοις.
paragraphs.translit: elaben tous hepta artous kai tous ichthyas kai eucharistēsas eklasen kai edidou tois mathētais hoi de mathētai tois ochlois.

paragraphs.text: And they all ate, and were filled: and they took up that which remained over of the broken pieces, seven baskets full.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἔφαγον πάντες καὶ ἐχορτάσθησαν, καὶ τὸ περισσεῦον τῶν κλασμάτων ἦραν ἑπτὰ σπυρίδας πλήρεις.
paragraphs.translit: kai ephagon pantes kai echortasthēsan, kai to perisseuon tōn klasmatōn ēran hepta spyridas plēreis.

paragraphs.text: And they that did eat were four thousand men, besides women and children.
paragraphs.original: οἱ δὲ ἐσθίοντες ἦσαν τετρακισχίλιοι ἄνδρες χωρὶς γυναικῶν καὶ παιδίων.
paragraphs.translit: hoi de esthiontes ēsan tetrakischilioi andres chōris gynaikōn kai paidiōn.

paragraphs.text: And he sent away the multitudes, and entered into the boat, and came into the borders of Magadan.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἀπολύσας τοὺς ὄχλους ἐνέβη εἰς τὸ πλοῖον, καὶ ἦλθεν εἰς τὰ ὅρια Μαγαδάν.
paragraphs.translit: kai apolysas tous ochlous enebē eis to ploion, kai ēlthen eis ta horia Magadan.
